The greenhouse gases are being produced by almost all human
activities, such as agriculture, cutting of trees, household usages
of refrigerators and air-conditioners, business activities like
burning of fossil fuels in industries and vehicles. As more fossil
fuels are burned, greenhouse gases enter the atmosphere and
trap more heat. Consequently greenhouses gases, especially
carbon dioxide levels rise in atmosphere and as a result,
temperature of the earth as a whole increases. This increase in
average temperature of the earth is called global warming.
Global warming

5.4 Impacts of GreenhouseGasses and Global Warming
The human-enhanced greenhouse effect and global warming are the main driving forces of
climate change.An increase in the greenhouse effect could prove devastating for life on earth in
many ways.This is highlighted through some facts below:
Between 1906 and 2005, average temperature of the earth increased by 0.74°C.
8 of the 10 warmest years on record occurred, since the year 2000.
